title: Do You Need Flood Insurance in Florida if You're Not in a Flood Zone?
dek: This week's rain flooded homes in Palm Bay, Melbourne and Daytona that sat outside FEMA's high risk zones. Here is what flood insurance costs outside those zones, what it covers, and what happens if you don't have it.
body:
Yes, for most homes on the Florida coast it is worth having, even outside a FEMA flood zone. A standard homeowners policy does not cover flood, and from 2014 to 2024 nearly one third of all federal flood insurance claims came from properties outside FEMA's high risk areas, according to FloodSmart, the federal flood insurance site.

This week showed why. Days of heavy rain from November 17 to 21 flooded streets and homes from Palm Bay and Melbourne up through Cocoa, Daytona Beach and Palm Coast. Spectrum News 13 reported homeowners in Palm Bay dealing with damage in neighborhoods that were never mapped as flood zones, and one Melbourne homeowner told the Associated Press her house flooded twice in two weeks.

Low flood risk on the map is not no flood risk

Our own flood rankings make the point. We scored 50 beach towns on two public maps: how much land the ocean reaches at high tide, and how much sits in FEMA's high risk zone. Palm Bay and Melbourne came out among the safest, 46th and 48th of 50. Only about 29% of Palm Bay and 21% of Melbourne is in a high risk zone, so most homeowners there are never required to buy flood insurance.

Both towns flooded this week anyway. Our rankings measure ocean and storm surge risk, and FEMA's maps mostly do too. Neither one captures what happens when days of heavy rain fall on neighborhoods built on flat, low ground with nowhere for the water to go. We cover that difference in Florida floods two ways.

These are the towns in our rankings where the least land sits in FEMA's high risk zone. They are good places to live, and they are exactly where people tend to skip flood coverage.

How much does flood insurance cost outside a flood zone?

Usually far less than people expect. Federal flood policies in Florida average about $1,000 a year, and homeowners in non coastal communities can often get coverage for about $50 to $60 a month, according to the Insurance Information Institute.

Get quotes from both the federal program (the National Flood Insurance Program, or NFIP) and private flood insurers. Florida has the biggest private flood insurance market in the country, with dozens of companies writing it, and the Insurance Information Institute recommends comparing both. An independent insurance agent can usually quote both in one call.

What does flood insurance cover?

A federal flood policy covers up to $250,000 for the house itself and up to $100,000 for your belongings. Building and contents coverage are bought separately and have separate deductibles, so if you only buy building coverage, your furniture, clothes and electronics are not covered. Private policies can go higher, which matters if your house would cost more than $250,000 to rebuild.

Your regular homeowners policy may still pay for water that comes in through a roof damaged by wind. Water that rises from the ground, a river or a flooded street is flood, and only a flood policy pays for it.

Can I buy flood insurance right before a storm?

Not if you want it to pay for that storm. A new federal flood policy usually takes 30 days to start. The main exception is a policy bought when you close on a mortgage, which starts at closing. That is the simplest time to add it: when you buy the house.

What happens if my home floods and I don't have flood insurance?

You pay for most of it yourself. FEMA grants are only available after a federal disaster declaration, and FEMA's cap for home repair and housing help is currently $44,800 for a single disaster. Most federal disaster help comes as low interest loans from the Small Business Administration, which have to be paid back.

By comparison, federal flood insurance claim payments averaged about $68,000 from 2016 to 2021, according to FloodSmart, and never have to be repaid. And if your home is in a high risk zone and you accept FEMA repair money after a flood, you are required to buy and keep flood insurance to qualify for help next time.

When are you required to have flood insurance in Florida?

  • High risk zone with a federally backed mortgage. If your home is in a zone starting with A or V on FEMA's map, your lender will require it.
  • Citizens policyholders. Florida law is phasing in a flood insurance requirement for homes insured by Citizens, the state backed insurer. Homes valued at $400,000 or more needed flood coverage by January 1, 2026, and every Citizens covered home will need it by 2027.
  • Everyone else. It is optional. Homes like the ones that flooded in Palm Bay this week often fall in this group.

Is federal flood insurance going away?

Not for now, but Congress keeps it on short extensions. The program is currently authorized through December 11, 2026. When it lapses, existing policies stay in force until they expire, but new policies and renewals stop until Congress acts, as happened for 43 days in October and November 2025. Private flood policies are not affected by a lapse.

How to check flood risk on a Florida home before you buy

  • Look up the address on FEMA's Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov) to see its zone.
  • Look up the evacuation zone at FloridaDisaster.org/Know. A home can be outside a flood zone and still inside a storm surge evacuation zone.
  • Ask the seller whether the house has ever flooded or had a flood claim, and ask for the current flood premium if there is one.
  • Drive the street after a heavy rain. Standing water at the curb tells you more than any map.
  • Get a flood quote before your inspection period ends, so it is part of what you pay, not a surprise after closing.

Our family has lived on this coast for 20 years, and the lesson is simple: the storm that floods your street is rarely the one you were watching on the map. Insure for water, not for the zone. For what the rest of your insurance costs, see homeowners insurance costs by county.
faq: Is flood insurance required in flood zone X in Florida?
No. Zone X is outside FEMA's high risk area, so lenders don't require it. It is still worth considering: nearly one third of federal flood claims from 2014 to 2024 came from outside high risk areas.
How much is flood insurance in Florida in zone X?
Often about $50 to $60 a month for homes outside coastal high risk areas, per the Insurance Information Institute. The Florida average for a federal flood policy is about $1,000 a year.
Does homeowners insurance cover flooding in Florida?
No. Standard homeowners policies exclude flood. You need a separate flood policy from the federal program or a private insurer.
How long does it take for flood insurance to start?
A new federal flood policy usually takes 30 days to take effect. A policy bought at a mortgage closing starts at closing.
Does FEMA pay for flood damage if I don't have flood insurance?
Only after a federal disaster declaration, and grants are capped at $44,800 for home repair and housing help. Most federal disaster aid is SBA loans that must be repaid.
